draft.title: Work health and safety law
card: Work health and safety (WHS) laws aim to protect people from injury and illness at work. In most Australian states and territories, including NSW, the main law is the Work Health and Safety Act 2011.
must provide a safe workplace. This includes safe equipment, safe work methods, training and supervision, and a way to find and manage risks.
must take reasonable care for their own safety and the safety of others. They must also follow reasonable safety instructions given by the employer.
A business that breaks WHS law can face heavy fines, and in serious cases prosecution of the business or its officers. Fines can apply even if no one has been hurt yet.
draft.remember: Employers must provide a safe workplace, workers must work safely, and breaches can bring heavy penalties.

a.q: Which action best shows an employer meeting its WHS duty?
opts: Training staff to use a machine and guarding its parts
Giving staff a bonus for working faster on the machine
Asking staff to buy their own safety gear and manage risks
Waiting for an injury before checking how the machine is used
a.why: An employer must provide safe equipment, training and a way to manage risks before harm happens. Waiting for an injury is tempting to some, but the duty is to act on risks first, and fines can apply even without an injury.
a.clue: The duty is to prevent harm, not to react to it.

b.q: Dani's warehouse in Parramatta gives staff safety training and high-visibility vests. A worker, Sam, ignores a clear instruction to stay out of a marked forklift zone and is nearly hit. Who has failed their WHS duty?
opts: Sam, who did not follow a reasonable safety instruction
Dani, who must stop every worker from ignoring instructions
Both equally, because duties fall on the employer alone
Neither, because no one was actually injured in the incident
b.why: Workers must follow reasonable safety instructions, so Sam has failed his duty. Dani did provide training and equipment, so blaming her alone is tempting but wrong. A near miss still counts, because the duty does not depend on an injury happening.
b.clue: Both employers and workers have duties, and Dani has met hers here.
